title: Reg.exe exports the SAM or SECURITY registry hive
description: Detects reg.exe save or export commands targeting the SAM or SECURITY registry hive, a process-visible path toward offline credential extraction.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may export local credential material from the SAM or SECURITY registry hive for offline processing.
hypothesis.rationale: MITRE explicitly documents reg save against these sensitive hives as a credential-dumping method; approved incident response and forensic acquisition can produce the same process command.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify reg.exe save or export actions with a bounded SAM or SECURITY source key, including subkeys, while excluding registry queries, similarly named hives and matches only in destination paths.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process events

triage.summary: Determine who exported the hive, where the output was written and whether the resulting credential material was accessed, staged or transferred.
steps: Review the complete command line, account, device, parent process, output path and nearby elevated process activity.
Inspect creation and access of the exported hive, subsequent archive or transfer behavior and credential-related tooling on the endpoint.
Confirm an approved forensic or recovery workflow; isolate the device, protect affected credentials and preserve evidence if unauthorized.
false_positives: Authorized forensic acquisition, incident response, backup or disaster-recovery activity

validation.expected_outcome: Match reg.exe save or export commands for the SAM or SECURITY hive; do not match queries, other hives, unrelated processes or missing command lines.

limitations: This single-event signal does not establish malicious intent or successful execution. Renamed binaries, alternate tools, obfuscation and unlogged activity can evade the bounded predicates.
Current-revision evidence is synthetic only. Validate full generated KQL, source fields, ingestion delay, alert volume and scoped exclusions in the target before enabling.
